grammar.change_scope: finalized uniform operator registration/overload semantics; required one source-only operator library block; typed all operator attributes; removed co.lang.operator from ordinary declaration kinds; adopted maximal-munch ASCII semantics

structural_checks.decision_sync_policy: Executable grammar decisions must occur in both the EBNF and register. Configuration, bootstrap-order, artifact-projection, ownership, conflict, conformance-profile, and withdrawn historical decisions may be reference/register-only when they do not change an executable production.

secondary_roots.reason: DECISION-OPDECL-004: dedicated operator-source grammar parsed before ordinary source

                             { parameter-list }, return-type-clause,

design_assertions.description: Local functions require a block definition and cannot be forward declarations.
Anonymous function, lambda, anonymous class and block forms are expressions.
Anonymous class expressions carry no declaration name.
forall is reachable through type-expression.
Ordinary function-declaration is not a direct package primary.
The grammar records declaration-site lexical scope for ordinary local functions.
The grammar records @co.dap.inner call-site lexical-context resolution.
Object construction is an expression and does not use body-close.
Pattern block bodies and expression results keep separate termination.
Direct anonymous function bindings use body termination.
Named UDT bodies use body-close.
Built-in directives are self-delimiting.
Enum variants are comma-separated.
Identifier production enforces ASCII-leading identifier shape.
Numeric literal productions do not admit apostrophe/underscore digit separators.
Boolean and none literals use co.const spellings.
Dependent indices use the dedicated index production; dependentType is a direct type kind, and a function-shaped type constructor has exactly one type-producing result (possibly one union).

evidence.type-constructor-primary:
annotations, function-name, parameter-list,
                           { parameter-list }, type-constructor-return-clause,
                           type-constructor-binding

design_assertions.description: Planned grammar constructs remain represented.
Built-in, pre-declared, and custom operator implementations all use mode=overload in legal function owners; distinct normalized signatures are permitted.
fol-conf.yaml configures operator_library_folder and the folder is excluded from package discovery.
operators.fol has exactly one @co.dap.library(type=operator) _ co.lang.library block containing only operator declarations.
Operator declaration attributes are typed; four parse attributes are required semantically and optional metadata keys are bounded to one occurrence.

evidence.operator-property: "fixity", annotation-binder, operator-fixity | "precedence", annotation-binder, decimal-integer-literal | "associativity", annotation-binder, operator-associativity | "arity", annotation-binder, operator-arity | "commutative", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "idempotent", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "identity", annotation-binder, operator-identity-value | "foldable", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "vectorizable", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "distributes_over", annotation-binder, operator-symbol-list

design_assertions.description: Pre-declared mathematical/modifier glyphs are language-owned registrations and may receive overload implementations.
Custom ASCII symbols use maximal munch; whitespace disambiguates adjacent shorter operators rather than triggering a collision error.
The operator source grammar is rooted at operator-source-file and is not reachable from compilation-unit.
co.lang.operator is absent from ordinary general-declarable-kind and appears only in the dedicated operator-source grammar.
Ordinary library artifacts and imports carry no operator table.
The alpha profile implements infix, prefix, and postfix custom operators; other fixities are reserved.

production_snapshot.body-closure-guard: ? zero-width condition: the next significant token is not ";", or there is no next token ?
production_snapshot.non-block-expression-guard: ? zero-width condition: the complete source span is not admissible as an unparenthesized block production; when both block and another braced expression are possible, the block reading has priority ?
production_snapshot.non-anonymous-function-expression-guard: ? zero-width condition: the complete source span is not admissible as an unparenthesized anonymous-function-expression production; that direct body reading has priority over the general expression reading ?
production_snapshot.primary-expression: literal | special-binding | "this" | "self" | qualified-name | grouped-expression | tuple-expression | array-literal | map-literal | object-construction | anonymous-class-expression | block | anonymous-function-expression | let-expression | comprehension-expression
production_snapshot.extended-operator-expression: ? expression containing a registered non-built-in operator, parsed by precedence climbing from its declared fixity, precedence, associativity, and arity; all built-in subexpressions obey the table above ?
production_snapshot.informative-mixed-chain: "(", expression, ")", informative-branch-verb, "(", block, ")", { ".otherwise", "(", expression, ")", informative-branch-verb, "(", block, ")" }, [ ".otherwise", informative-branch-verb, "(", block, ")" ]
production_snapshot.builtin-literal: integer-literal | floating-literal | string-literal-sequence | character-literal | boolean-literal | none-literal
production_snapshot.integer-suffix: unsigned-suffix, [ long-suffix | long-long-suffix | size-suffix ] | long-suffix, [ unsigned-suffix ] | long-long-suffix, [ unsigned-suffix ] | size-suffix, [ unsigned-suffix ]
production_snapshot.decimal-floating-literal: fractional-constant, [ exponent-part ], [ floating-point-suffix ] | decimal-digit-sequence, exponent-part, [ floating-point-suffix ]
production_snapshot.alpha-basic-c-character: ? any translation character except apostrophe, backslash, carriage return, or line feed ?
production_snapshot.alpha-basic-s-character: ? any translation character except double quote, backslash, carriage return, or line feed ?
production_snapshot.identifier-trailing-guard: ? a zero-width assertion that the next character is not "_" ?
production_snapshot.reserved-future-operator: ? one character from the hard-reserved future syntax set, explicitly excluding every language-predeclared operator glyph; unavailable for use, declaration, or overload ?
production_snapshot.line-comment: "//", { ? any Unicode scalar value except CR or LF ? }
production_snapshot.block-comment-character: ? any Unicode scalar value that does not begin the two-character sequence */ ?
production_snapshot.operator-property: "fixity", annotation-binder, operator-fixity | "precedence", annotation-binder, decimal-integer-literal | "associativity", annotation-binder, operator-associativity | "arity", annotation-binder, operator-arity | "commutative", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "idempotent", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "identity", annotation-binder, operator-identity-value | "foldable", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "vectorizable", annotation-binder, boolean-literal | "distributes_over", annotation-binder, operator-symbol-list
production_snapshot.operator-symbol: ? a maximal run of one or more symbol characters, where a symbol character is any character that is not an ASCII letter, digit, underscore, whitespace, or one of the delimiters ( ) { } [ ] , ; " ' ; the run must not be a language-owned or hard-reserved symbol and must not begin with // or /* ?

notes: Operator registration and implementation are separate: custom symbols are registered once; all implementations use mode=overload.
The fixed operators.fol surface is one source-only @co.dap.library(type=operator) _ co.lang.library block.
Pre-declared glyphs are language-owned and overloadable; hard-reserved spellings remain unavailable.
ASCII custom symbols obey maximal munch; whitespace disambiguates adjacent shorter operators.
No operator metadata crosses ordinary library boundaries.
